context: Restore green by whichever route the reviewer prefers on #1543, then fix the misreporting, which is the part that will otherwise cost the next person the same hour.
description: On a clean checkout of 916d9533ab the agent instruction audit reports active instruction bytes 16088 against a 16000 budget - 88 bytes over, from #1541. That fails three tests in tests/unit/scripts/test_agent_instruction_audit.py and the agent-identity-check make target (measured exit 2). It runs as a pre-commit hook, so it blocks every commit in every worktree; this session's own commit needed SKIP=agent-git-identity. Auto-revert PR #1543 already exists and would restore green by reverting #1541. The durable defect is separate: the hook surfaces this as a stale Git identity failure while the real cause is the byte budget, which cost real diagnosis time before the true cause was found.

work_units.evidence: Moved the 'Audit evidence provenance' section out of docs/development/agent-review-protocol.md into a new docs/development/audit-evidence-provenance.md, leaving a two-line pointer. It is a records convention for _project/audits/*.md enforced mechanically by audit_sha_check.py, not review behaviour every session must carry, so it does not belong in the always-loaded surface. active_bytes 16088 -> 14989 against a 16000 budget: 1011 bytes of headroom rather than the 88-byte squeeze a wording trim would have bought. make agent-identity-check now exits 0 (was 2). No anchor, policy ID, or scenario text was touched; no doc links to the moved section by anchor and audit_sha_check.py remains the enforcing authority. Budget deliberately NOT raised.
work_units.summary: Restore develop green by landing the revert or by bringing active bytes under budget

work_units.evidence: Every audit error is now tagged with the check that produced it (budget, surface, review-policy, commit-policy, scenarios, git-identity, commit-range) via _tag(), and main() prints 'agent-instructions: FAIL (<checks>)' plus a failing_checks field in --json. The pre-commit hook keeps id agent-git-identity but is renamed 'agent instruction + Git identity audit', because pre-commit prints the hook NAME, not the command, on failure - that name was the misreport. Verified: forcing active_bytes over budget prints 'FAIL (budget)' and 'ERROR: budget: active instruction bytes ... exceed budget', where develop previously printed a hook named 'reject stale agent Git identity'. Existing tests assert error substrings rather than equality, so the prefix does not break them: 48 passed.
work_units.summary: Make the hook name the check that actually failed instead of reporting a Git identity failure

work_units.evidence: Added budget_headroom_warnings(): any budgeted metric at or above 97 percent of its ceiling reports how many units remain. Deliberately a warning, never an error - a second failing threshold would just be a lower budget, and main() already excludes warnings from exit status. #1541 crossed a 16000-byte ceiling by 88 bytes with no prior signal; at 97 percent the warning would have fired from 15520 onward. It fires today on a real near-full metric: 'AGENTS.md lines 167 is within 3 of the 170 budget'. Four new tests cover attribution, headroom firing near the ceiling, silence with room to spare, and the hook name; 48 passed, ruff clean on both changed Python files.
work_units.summary: Give the budget a visible margin so a small docs edit cannot red develop again
